messages:
alex_riordan: quick heads-up — found a mismatch between py/ts SDKs around the `stop` param serialization.
priya: details?
alex_riordan: python client sends `stop=None` which serializes to `null` in the JSON body. TS client leaves `stop` `undefined` so the field is omitted. server treats `null` as explicit 'clear' and errors in some endpoints.
sam: ah, that explains the 400s I saw in canary tests yesterday. which endpoint?
alex_riordan: /v1/generate (text generation). behaviour: if stop === null -> server tries to coerce into list and 400s with "stop must be array of strings". if omitted -> server uses model-defaults.
tia: can we make server accept null as omit? or better to normalize in SDKs?
kevin: prefer SDK-level fix + acceptance on server for backward-compat. server change risks touching lots of clients.
priya: agree with SDK-first. quick friction: python idiom uses None to mean 'not set' while TS uses undefined. both are reasonable but need consistent wire semantics.
sam: proposed options: 1) py: don't emit key when value is None; 2) server: treat null as omit; 3) accept both and document.
kevin: option 1 simplest for short term. We already have a pattern in other flags (e.g., `max_tokens`) where py omits None. seems like a regression introduced by recent serialization change in py-sdk.
alex_riordan: OK i'll open a tiny PR to change py-serializer to drop None for optional list/string params. will add a unit test matching TS behaviour. PR WIP: https://git.internal.redwood/pr/4821
priya: add a changelog note and call out compatibility for existing users. also add an integration test hitting /v1/generate that asserts body does not include `stop` when None.
tia: pinging @deploy-bot — any canary alerts tied to these 400s?
deploy-bot: canary-alert: /v1/generate 400-rate spike +0.9% between 03:14-03:22 UTC. Linked traces: trace/0a9f3.
sam: good to have that trace; will grab payload and see if it matches `stop:null`.
kevin: cross-check: do we have similar behavior for `stream` boolean? py currently sends `stream:false` always, TS omits if undefined. maybe we should standardize for booleans too.
priya: we should create a short SDK-interop checklist: param omitted vs null, empty-list vs null vs omitted, enum casing, date formats. add to eng-platform docs.
alex_riordan: created doc stub: docs/sdks/interop-checklist.md in my branch. will link in PR.
sam: timeline?
alex_riordan: aiming to land py fix + tests today, cut patch release tomorrow morning. server tolerant change can follow if we decide to be defensive.
tia: FYI also saw TS typed examples that still include camelCase `maxTokens` in quickstarts vs our REST expects `max_tokens`. SDKs translate that, but double-check mapping is bi-directional for telemetry.
kevin: good catch. ensure telemetry-normalizer maps both forms to canonical metric keys.
priya: next steps: alex opens PR (done), sam adds an integration test referencing deploy trace, tia files a tiny doc update, kevin to approve server-side tolerant change if needed.
alex_riordan: PR: https://git.internal.redwood/pr/4821 — note: patch changes serializer.emit_if_not_none for list/str types. test added: tests/test_generate_payload.py::test_omit_stop_when_none
sam: LGTM pending CI. I'll queue the canary test after patch lands.
tia: once patch is out, I'll run staging attach tests with legacy clients.
kevin: flagging for release notes: "SDK: Python client now omits unset optional params to match TS/REST contract (fixes spurious 400s on /v1/generate)"
alex_riordan: thanks all. follow-up: create a tiny server acceptance test to treat `null` same as omitted for one release window — open issue #893.
priya: added #893 to backlog and labeled `interop` + `p1` (temporary).
kevin: closing loop: make sure analytics doesn't treat omitted vs null as different events.
priya: noted. will sync with analytics team.
kevin: thanks, thread resolved for now :thumbsup:
